mainTopic: Can a man who is only engaged (ארוס) cancel his bride's vows alone once the waiting period before the wedding has passed and he must now support her?
overview: The משנה brings a מחלוקת about a בוגרת or a widow whose waiting time before the wedding has passed. רבי אליעזר says that since her ארוס must already support her, he may cancel her vows by himself. חכמים say he cannot until she actually enters his home. רבה links רבי אליעזר to the משנה ראשונה in כתובות, which let such a bride eat תרומה once the twelve months were over. A later court changed that rule and required the חופה first. אביי rejects the link from both sides. The משנה ראשונה may have been lenient only about תרומה, which is rabbinic, and not about vows, which are from the Torah. רבי אליעזר may be lenient only about vows, because a woman vows with her husband in mind, and he might not let her eat even rabbinic תרומה.

steps.title: Can the engaged man cancel her vows once the wedding date has passed?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings a מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and חכמים about a bride whose waiting period before the wedding is over.
steps.simpleTranslation: A grown woman who waited twelve months after her engagement, or a widow who waited thirty days: רבי אליעזר says that since her husband must already feed her, he may cancel her vows. חכמים say the husband cannot cancel until she enters his domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes a bride whose waiting period before the wedding is finished but who has not yet married. It brings two opinions on whether her ארוס alone can cancel her vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an ארוס can cancel vows only together with her father. A בוגרת or a widow is no longer under her father's control, so before the wedding her ארוס would have no power over her vows at all. רבי אליעזר says that once the ארוס must support her, he counts like a full husband and can cancel alone. חכמים say only actually entering his domain, meaning the חופה, gives him that power.

keyTerms.meaning: A grown woman, past the age of being under her father's control
A widow
Food and support that a husband owes his wife
He may cancel (her vows)
His domain or control, meaning his home after the wedding

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ בּוֹגֶרֶת שֶׁשָּׁהֲתָה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: MISHNA: A grown woman who waited twelve months
phrases.notes: These are the twelve months after her engagement, the time she is given to get ready for the wedding.

phrases.english: and a widow who waited thirty days,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
Since her husband is obligated to support her, he may cancel her vows.
But the Rabbis say:
The husband does not cancel
until she enters his domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בּוֹגֶרֶת שֶׁשָּׁהֲתָה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: the obligation to support her gives the ארוס power to cancel her vows alone. חכמים: only after she enters his domain.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the question the rest of the גמרא explores: does the duty to support her make him count as a husband?

steps.title: רבה links רבי אליעזר to the earlier version of a משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבה claims that רבי אליעזר holds the same view as the משנה ראשונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: רבי אליעזר and the first version of the משנה said the same thing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה says that רבי אליעזר is not alone. His view matches an earlier version of a משנה, which the גמרא is about to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions share one idea. Once the waiting time has passed and the man must support her, she is already treated like his wife in some ways. The proof comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The first or earlier version of a משנה, later changed by a later court
The same thing, one idea

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabba says:
Rabbi Eliezer and the initial version of the mishna
said the same thing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וּמִשְׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי אליעזר's view in the משנה by connecting it to an older source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר's opinion matches the משנה ראשונה.

steps.title: The quoted משנה: after twelve months she eats his food and תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה in כתובות: after twelve months the bride is supported by the ארוס and may eat תרומה, but a יבם does not let her eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: a virgin is given twelve months to prepare herself. Once twelve months arrive, she eats from his food and eats תרומה. But a יבם does not let her eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting the source behind רבה's claim. It shows that after twelve months the ארוס must feed her, and if he is a כהן, she may even eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being allowed to eat תרומה means she is treated like a כהן's wife even before the חופה. This matches רבי אליעזר's idea that the duty to support her makes her like his wife. A יבם is different: he does not give her this right until they actually marry.

keyTerms.meaning: To prepare herself, getting her things ready for the wedding
The holy portion of produce that only כהנים and their households may eat
The brother of a man who died without children, who must marry or release the widow
Allows her to eat

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: A virgin is given
twelve months to prepare herself.
Once the twelve months arrived,
she eats from his food, and she eats terumah.
phrases.notes: The תרומה part applies when the man she is engaged to is a כהן.

phrases.english: But a yavam does not let her eat terumah.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: נוֹתְנִין לַבְּתוּלָה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ לְפַרְנֵס עַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that רבה relies on.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's claim that רבי אליעזר matches the משנה ראשונה
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in כתובות: after twelve months the bride eats his food and תרומה

steps.title: Partial time does not count, and the later court changed the rule
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה adds that the twelve months must be complete under one man. It identifies this as the משנה ראשונה, which a later court changed to require the חופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she spent six months waiting for the husband and six months waiting for the יבם, or even all of them for the husband minus one day, or all of them for the יבם minus one day, she does not eat תרומה. This is the first version of the משנה. A later court said: a woman does not eat תרומה until she enters the חופה.
steps.whatsHappening: The quote continues and shows that the rule only works after a full twelve months waiting for the ארוס himself. Then it tells us this was the משנה ראשונה, which a later court changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line is what tells us the earlier ruling is called the משנה ראשונה, the exact name רבה used. The later court held, like חכמים in our משנה, that only the חופה makes her a wife for this purpose. So רבי אליעזר fits the older ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Waiting for the husband, during the time she was engaged to him
Missing one day
A court that came after them, a later generation
The marriage canopy, the step that completes the marriage

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the later court is arguing about vows. It changed the rule only about eating תרומה. רבה is the one connecting it to our משנה about vows.

phrases.english: If she spent six months waiting for the husband,
and six months waiting for the yavam,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ כּוּלָּן בִּפְנֵי הַבַּעַל חָסֵר יוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: or even all of them waiting for the husband, minus one day,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ כּוּלָּן בִּפְנֵי הַיָּבָם חָסֵר יוֹם אֶחָד —
phrases.english: or all of them waiting for the yavam, minus one day,
she does not eat terumah.
This is the initial version of the mishna.
A court that came after them said:
The woman does not eat terumah
until she enters the wedding canopy.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ מִשְׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה. בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל אַחֲרֵיהֶם אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quote and names the earlier ruling the משנה ראשונה, which completes רבה's proof.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's claim that רבי אליעזר matches the משנה ראשונה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling that she eats תרומה after twelve months is labeled the משנה ראשונה, which a later court reversed.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ראשונה treated a bride as a wife once the twelve months were over. The later court required the חופה. רבה lines רבי אליעזר up with the first view.

steps.title: אביי: תרומה is rabbinic, but vows are from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רבה's link. The משנה ראשונה may have been lenient only about תרומה, which is a rabbinic matter, and not about vows, which are a Torah matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Maybe it is not so. The משנה ראשונה only taught us about eating תרומה, which is rabbinic. But vows are from the Torah, so say that it does not apply to them.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי argues that the proof does not work. The משנה ראשונה could agree with חכמים about vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on an engaged woman eating תרומה is only rabbinic, so the rabbis of the משנה ראשונה could relax it after twelve months. Cancelling vows touches a Torah law, so the same people may not have given the ארוס that power. The משנה ראשונה therefore does not prove that anyone held like רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps it is not so
It only taught us this far and no further
Of rabbinic law
Of Torah law

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common move in the גמרא. A leniency in a rabbinic area cannot automatically be stretched to a Torah area.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Perhaps it is not so.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא אַשְׁמְעִינַן מִשְׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה
phrases.english: The initial version of the mishna teaches us only
about eating terumah, which is a rabbinic matter.
But vows, which are from the Torah,
say that it does not apply.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי, דִּלְמָא לָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבה's claim that the משנה ראשונה matches רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the link between רבי אליעזר and the משנה ראשונה, not the משנה ראשונה itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבה compared a rabbinic matter (תרומה) to a Torah matter (vows). A leniency in one does not prove a leniency in the other.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר may only be talking about vows, not תרומה
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes his rejection of רבה. רבי אליעזר may give the ארוס power over vows only because a woman vows with her husband in mind. About תרומה, he might not let her eat even rabbinic תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the only place we have heard רבי אליעזר's view is about vows. That fits what רב פנחס said in the name of רבא: every woman who makes a vow makes it with her husband's consent in mind. But about תרומה, even rabbinic תרומה, she may not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues his rejection of רבה from the other direction. Step 5 limited the משנה ראשונה to תרומה, and now he limits רבי אליעזר to vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said the two opinions match because both treat the bride as almost married once her twelve months are over. אביי says each one may have its own separate reason. רבי אליעזר lets the ארוס cancel her vows because of רב פנחס's rule that she vows with him in mind, and that reason says nothing about תרומה. So we cannot prove that the two opinions are the same.

keyTerms.meaning: "You only heard him say this here": the opinion is limited to this one case
Regarding vows
With her husband's consent in mind
From rabbinic law (not Torah law)
רב פנחס quoting רבא

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's rejection has two sides. The משנה ראשונה may be lenient only about rabbinic תרומה (step 5), and רבי אליעזר may be lenient only about vows, because a woman vows with her husband in mind (step 6). Since each may have its own reason, רבה's claim that they match is not proven.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two directions. In this step רבי אליעזר is the stricter one about תרומה. He might not let her eat even rabbinic תרומה, which is more than the משנה ראשונה allows.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: two rulings that look alike may come from completely different reasons, so one cannot be used to prove the other.

phrases.english: And until here you have not heard him
phrases.notes: He means this is the only area where we actually know רבי אליעזר's view.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer [say this] except regarding vows
like Rav Pinchas in the name of Rava
who said: any woman who vows
vows with her husband's consent in mind
But terumah
even rabbinic [terumah], she also does not eat

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן לָא שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אֶלָּא גַּבֵּי נְדָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's rejection from step 5. Step 5 limited the משנה ראשונה to תרומה, and this step limits רבי אליעזר to vows.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבה's claim (step 2) that רבי אליעזר holds like the משנה ראשונה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבה assumed both opinions come from one shared reason. In fact רבי אליעזר's ruling on vows may rest only on רב פנחס's rule that a woman vows with her husband in mind, which has nothing to do with תרומה.
